title: Concepts of Social Stratification
text:
Social stratification refers to a system by which groups within a society are categorized into distinct layers, creating unequal distribution of resources and power. These systems establish hierarchies based on factors such as wealth, occupation, education, and inherited status.

Theoretical perspectives suggest that stratification can be maintained through various mechanisms. Some models emphasize ascribed status—those characteristics given at birth, such as caste—while others focus on achieved status, which is earned through individual effort or skill acquisition. The relationship between economic capital (assets) and cultural capital (knowledge and connections) remains a central point of sociological study when analyzing mobility between these strata.

Furthermore, the institutionalization of inequality is key; societal norms, legal structures, and educational systems often reproduce existing class divisions across generations, thereby reinforcing structural disadvantages.
